name: goyaml-typetable
instr:
**Accented customer names come out garbled when our Go service loads the Python export**

Our CRM is Python and writes the customer list every night with `yaml.safe_dump(customers)`
(PyYAML 6, default options). Our Go sync service loads that file with this library into a
`[]Customer`, a struct of ours where a couple of fields are our own types. Every customer with
an accent in their name or city arrives mangled (José Müller from Zürich, for one): the accented
letters are gone, mostly with an invisible control character in their place, and that breaks our
CSV exports. Names without accents come through fine, and loading the same file back in Python
gives the right names, so the file itself looks okay.

The checkout is in /workdir. Could you track down where this actually goes wrong and fix it
there? Please include a regression test, as a _test.go file in the package it exercises (say
./repro_test.go), that fails on the current code because of this problem (a real test failure,
not an import error) and passes once it's fixed.
Test the reported behaviour, not your patch: it should still pass if the bug gets fixed some other correct
way, so no asserting on source text or on helpers only your fix has. It should run on its own
from a clean checkout with just your test files added.

I doubt I'm the only one hitting this. Anything else that goes through that code is probably
wrong too, so please fix it at the source rather than special-casing my input. The fix belongs in
the library
